    A separate SYSREF lane is not needed: the SYSREF edge rides on the CLK cable, PG269 sets no transport rule, and CHAIN-TS gives a true SYSREF on the chain cables. Parts and nets: Carrier schematic.

    Engineering notes Decisions: LMK00804B buffers, U21 removal, TRIG over PERST#

    LMK1D → LMK00804B (U20, U22, U28)

    The earlier carrier plan used LMK1D-class parts for U20 and U22, with "one LVCMOS output" on U22. The LMK1D family has LVDS outputs only. One LVDS leg into the card's 49.9 Ω R348 gives ≈ 0.18 Vpp, below the 0.25 Vpp CLKin minimum, and there is no LVCMOS drive for the SYNC pin on J64.

    Decision: U20, U22 and U28 are LMK00804B (LVCMOS outputs, ≈ 1.65 Vpp at J35; U22 VDDO 2.5 V from U60, so the SYNC pin stays clear of the LMK abs max). U27 stays LMK1D1204 with its input in differential mode (0.3 Vpp, to 2 GHz). Status: fixed on the carrier.

    U21 removal

    No carrier has its own LMK04828 any more. The root makes LOCAL5 from Y1 (10 MHz TCXO with OE) and U29 (÷ 2); only the root turns them on. Every carrier is the same build; the role is a U30 register setting.

    J42, W24 and W25 removal

    TRIG IO moves off J64 to the slot pin PERST# (A11 → R242 0 Ω → FPGA D9), with D11, U62 and 33 Ω on the carrier: no card work and no W25. J42 and its cable W24 are removed with U23, U24 and JP2 (decision A); J65 IO3 is SYNC_GATE.

    The corrections this study found sit with their owners: the card rows in Card findings, the clock and SYNC path in Sync & trigger.

    Engineering notes Ethernet and RS-485 backup, E2 dropped

    Keep the external switch with N + 1 ports: a dead module never cuts the others off, and it carries the profiles to every module. The on-carrier switch option (E2) is dropped so every carrier stays one build. The two RS-485 ports on each card can carry a slow backup link along the chain.

    Engineering notes Mixing with a ZCU216

    The ZCU216's CLK104 can take CLK and SYSREF from the same sync unit, adding 16 DAC channels to the array. It needs its own front end (an RFMC mezzanine), and its outputs will differ slightly from the HamGeek channels, so calibrate it as a separate group.

    Engineering notes CLK input level budget per sync option

    Level budget at the LMK00804B inputs (estimate, to measure): J29 drives 1.65 Vpp into 50 Ω, the input tap takes 3 dB and each splitter stage 10·log10 n + 1 dB. The input window after the tap is 0.25–1.3 Vpp (LMK00804B, check).

    Master + splitter, 4 modules1:4 ZFSC-4-10.52 VppPASS
    Master + splitter, 8 modules1:2 + 1:4 ZSC-2-1+ → ZFSC-4-10.33 VppPASS
    Master + splitter, 8 modules, wide-band 1:8 option1:8 ZCSC-8-152-S+0.37 VppPASS
    Master + 2 splitters (legacy), 4 modules1:2 + 1:4 ZSC-2-1+ → ZFSC-4-10.33 VppPASS

    Only square sources: the splitters must pass ≤ 1 MHz to ≥ 500 MHz so the 5 MHz edges stay fast, which rules out ZFSC-8-1 (0.5–175 MHz) and ZFSC-2-1 (5–500 MHz). The live level for the current option is in Sync & trigger.

    TRIG (rear PCB jack J28 → D11 → U62 → 33 Ω → slot A11 PERST# → FPGA D9) must land inside one SYSREF period. The arm margins are drawn in the waves and the DC level at D9 is a status in Sync & trigger. Above 4 modules use an active TRIG fan-out, the sync unit's TRIG outputs or the GNSS-armed start (which needs U101 fitted on every card).

    Upright box, rd2 legend (front outputs)

    16 SMA bulkheads in two rows (RF-DAC 1–8 on top, one-bit 1–8 below), each fed by a short cable W1–W16 with an SMPM plug at the board edge. The SMA flanges did not fit at the 7 mm strip pitch, so they sat on the panel. Each cable rose straight out of its plug, stepped back to its own layer (one-bit cables in front, RF-DAC cables 11 mm behind), crossed over and ran straight into the SMA plug: bends of 5 mm radius or more, at least 0.3 mm between any two cables at every card length.

    Rear SMAs CLK IN (J26), SYSREF IN (J27), TRIG IO (J28) and CLK/SYSREF OUT (J29), each with a short cable (W17–W20; W19 ≈ 60 mm) to the carrier jacks in the clock zone. W21 ≈ 380 mm and W22 ≈ 390 mm at the 235 mm card (≈ 305–475 mm for 160–320 mm cards); W23 card J32 → carrier J45. W19 and W21–W23 stayed plugged in every sync option.

    Flat box, rd2 legend

    The card lay component side up in J1 on the L-shaped carrier. The RF-DAC rows started in front of the card's DAC jacks (eight identical 80 mm jumpers D0–D7, upright ≈ 260 mm), three one-bit strips started in front of J1 and five beside their own lane pins (lanes 17–48 mm, upright ≈ 91 mm), and the CLK, SYNC and GTY reference jumpers shrank to 45–80 mm. The U-cover (lid and both walls) lifted off; a lid baffle at x 46 kept the heatsink exhaust off the one-bit arm and two 40 mm rear fans pulled the air out.
